CLAIM_7_no_auth_usage.claim: uellix_app lacks USAGE ON SCHEMA auth.
CLAIM_7_no_auth_usage.evidence: Static: no GRANT ... ON SCHEMA auth TO uellix_app / uellix_writer / uellix_auditor exists anywhere in db/**. The five auth-schema grants in db/prepared/** all target a DEDICATED capability role (uellix_cap_invitation, uellix_cap_bootstrap, uellix_cap_platform, uellix_cap_stella_quota, uellix_cap_stella_ticket), never a broad runtime role. CLAIM_8_42501_at_trigger_execution.claim: The failure is SQLSTATE 42501 raised at trigger execution.
CLAIM_8_42501_at_trigger_execution.evidence: P1C verbatim: 'ERROR: 42501: permission denied for schema auth / LINE 1: v_actor := auth.uid() / QUERY: v_actor := auth.uid() / CONTEXT: PL/pgSQL function enforce_organization_commercial_acceptance_invariants() line 22 at assignment'.
CLAIM_8_42501_at_trigger_execution.WHY_THE_POLICY_SURVIVES_WHAT_THE_BODY_DO: MEASURED ASYMMETRY, and the single most important finding in this section. The INSERT policy's WITH CHECK contains a DIRECT auth.uid() (0072:116). If THAT expression also required schema USAGE, the defect would not be trigger-scoped and no trigger-scoped remediation could make PG-06 satisfiable. P2A proves it does not: with the trigger disabled and the policy fully armed, the same runtime role in the same identity context inserted successfully. A STORED policy expression was name-resolved at CREATE time and is executed against stored OIDs, so at run time PostgreSQL checks EXECUTE on the function and never re-checks USAGE on the schema. A PL/pgSQL body parses its SQL expressions at RUNTIME in the calling session, so name resolution -- and therefore schema USAGE -- IS checked against the invoker. P8C isolates the other half: after REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION auth.uid() FROM PUBLIC the stored policy fails with '42501: permission denied for function uid'. EXECUTE is what a stored policy needs; USAGE is what a PL/pgSQL body additionally needs.
CLAIM_8_42501_at_trigger_execution.CONSEQUENCE_BINDING: The defect is TRIGGER-SCOPED. A remediation confined to the trigger function is SUFFICIENT, and no policy, no grant and no role needs to change.

CLAIM_9_other_13_unaffected.claim: The other 13 PG-06 INSERT relations do not share this defect.
CLAIM_9_other_13_unaffected.evidence: A trigger census over db/migrations/**, db/policies/** and db/prepared/** for all 14 PG-06 INSERT relations returns exactly THREE triggers that can fire on INSERT: (a) account_legal_acceptances BEFORE INSERT -> enforce_account_legal_acceptance_invariants (0070:205) -- INVOKER, but its body names NO auth.uid(); it reads only legal_instrument_versions and legal_instruments, which the runtime holds SELECT on, so it is correct as INVOKER; (b) organization_commercial_acceptances BEFORE INSERT -> enforce_organization_commercial_acceptance_invariants (0072:234) -- THE DEFECT; (c) outcome_monetization_dispositions BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE -> uellix_guard_disposition_run_approval (0060:107) -- ALREADY SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public (0060:67-72). The remaining 11 relations carry no INSERT-firing trigger at all (only BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE append-only guards on two of them).
CLAIM_9_other_13_unaffected.note: 0070 is the instructive near-miss: same authorship idiom, same INVOKER mode, same two registry reads -- and CORRECT, because it never reaches schema auth. The discriminator is the auth reach, not the privilege mode in isolation.

OPTION_B_security_definer_plus_pinned_se.in_repo_precedent: db/migrations/0060:67-72 -- CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION uellix_guard_disposition_run_approval() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public. A BEFORE INSERT trigger function on another PG-06 relation, in the same corpus, already in exactly this form.
OPTION_B_security_definer_plus_pinned_se.WHY_THE_search_path_PIN_IS_LOAD_BEARING_: This was tested rather than asserted, and the first result contradicted the generic rationale. With the pin REMOVED and SECURITY DEFINER kept, a caller-controlled search_path did NOT shadow the registries (P6D, P7A) -- because search_path resolution SILENTLY SKIPS schemas the EFFECTIVE user lacks USAGE on, and inside a DEFINER function the effective user is the OWNER. Granting the OWNER usage on the attacker-writable schema flipped it: with the pin still removed, the shadowed registry WAS used and a FORGED content_digest was accepted and stored, defeating I-T4-4 (P7B, INSERT 0 1 with content_digest sha256:dead...). Restoring the pin refused the identical attack (P7C). CONCLUSION: the pin is the decisive barrier, with the precise precondition that the owner can see a schema the attacker can write to. A second, independent barrier was also measured: the runtime role holds no CREATE on schema public (P6A, has_schema_privilege(app,public,CREATE)=f). Both are real; neither is a reason to omit the other.

OPTION_C_use_an_existing_identity_doorwa.reason: MEASURED: a census of every SECURITY DEFINER function in db/migrations/** and db/policies/** returns ZERO that return the acting subject's scalar uuid. The three existing doorways return uuid[] (current_user_org_ids), text (current_user_role_in_org) and boolean (current_user_is_super_admin). I-T4-6 requires the SUBJECT IDENTITY ITSELF for the accepted_by_user_id equality, which none of them yields. Note that the trigger ALREADY uses a doorway correctly for the role half -- public.current_user_role_in_org(NEW.organization_id) at 0072:209 never fails, because it is SECURITY DEFINER. The defect is confined to the one obligation no existing doorway can serve.
OPTION_C_use_an_existing_identity_doorwa.residual_value: This option is not merely rejected: it explains the defect. The author reached for a doorway where one existed and reached for auth.uid() directly where none did.

OPTION_D_create_a_new_identity_helper.privilege_expansion: Creates a NEW persistent public function, which then needs its own REVOKE, its own EXECUTE posture, its own ownership and its own closed-world accounting.
OPTION_D_create_a_new_identity_helper.effect_on_ACL_authority: MATERIAL. A new public function is a new surface the current-schema closed-world guard and the runtime ACL contract must both account for.
OPTION_D_create_a_new_identity_helper.decisive_reason: It achieves exactly what option B achieves, at the cost of a new permanent object in the public schema and a wider write set. Option B changes the privilege mode of a function that already exists; option D adds one. Narrowest wins.

OPTION_E_remove_the_actor_invariant.decisive_reason: It deletes I-T4-6 and I-T4-7 -- the obligations the unit exists to enforce -- to make a privilege error disappear. It would leave accepted_by_user_id and accepted_by_role client-supplied and unverified at the database boundary, which is precisely the property 0072's own prose calls the reason the trigger exists at all ('a trigger binds every writer, including the table owner and a superuser'). This is weakening a control to obtain a PASS and is refused under the fail-closed rule.

SELECTION.SELECTED_REMEDIATION: B -- SECURITY DEFINER + SET search_path = public on enforce_organization_commercial_acceptance_invariants(), in the db/migrations/0060:67-72 precedent form, with NO grant of USAGE ON SCHEMA auth to any runtime role.

SECTION_5_OWNER_TOPOLOGY.NO_ALTER_OWNER_IS_PINNED: BINDING. This authority does NOT pin any ALTER FUNCTION ... OWNER TO statement, and the remediation MUST NOT introduce one. MEASURED (P3A): CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION on an existing function PRESERVES its owner -- owner_before and owner_after were identical across the remediation -- so the correct owner is inherited from whoever applied the migration, exactly as today.

REQUIRED_OWNER_CAPABILITY.must_resolve_auth_uid: The effective owner/applier context must hold USAGE ON SCHEMA auth. On the hosted baseline uellix_owner already does (db/baseline/stella_g2_schema.sql:9920).
REQUIRED_OWNER_CAPABILITY.must_preserve_I_T4_6_and_I_T4_7: The guards are carried verbatim; the owner change of mode must not alter which values are accepted.

SECTION_5_OWNER_TOPOLOGY.BOTH_REACHES_ARE_REQUIRED_AND_THE_FIRST_: MEASURED. Re-homing the repaired DEFINER function to an owner holding NEITHER auth USAGE nor registry SELECT turned the positive insert RED with '42501: permission denied for table legal_instrument_versions' at PL/pgSQL line 5 (P5A). Granting that owner auth USAGE and NOTHING else left it RED with the SAME table error (P5B). The registry read at 0072:167-171 executes BEFORE the auth.uid() assignment at 0072:198, so an owner-capability defect surfaces as a TABLE error, never as an auth error. A proof that only checks the owner's auth reach is therefore INSUFFICIENT, and a mutation that re-homes the function will not produce the error an auth-focused assertion is waiting for.
SECTION_5_OWNER_TOPOLOGY.A_TEST_SUBSTRATE_THAT_WIDENS_RUNTIME_IS_: BINDING. The owner capability must be satisfied by granting the OWNER what the hosted baseline already gives it -- never by granting a runtime role anything. Any fixture that makes the positive control pass by widening uellix_app, uellix_writer or uellix_auditor is INVALID EVIDENCE and must be refused by the certifier, whatever colour it produces.
SECTION_5_OWNER_TOPOLOGY.REAL_PG_PROOF_REQUIRED: The implementation must prove the owner capability on the governed substrate, not assume it. See SECTION_10 FUNCTION and SECTION_8 FIXTURE_DELTA.

SECTION_6_MIGRATION_VEHICLE.WHY_NOT_A_SUCCESSOR_MIGRATION: BROADER, and broader in a way that persists. A successor would add a permanent unit (ordinal 87) to the baseline order, would leave the DEFECTIVE text of 0072 in the chain to be applied first on every fresh provision, and would make the correct end-state depend on two units applying in order instead of one being right. Because 0072 has never been applied hosted, there is no historical application the in-place amendment could contradict -- the precise condition baseline unit 64's own managedNote relies on for its safety argument.
SECTION_6_MIGRATION_VEHICLE.WHY_NOT_A_PREPARED_PACKAGE: It would leave the DRIZZLE CHAIN DEFECTIVE. db/migrations is the Drizzle-generated lineage that local provisioning and the baseline units both consume; a prepared package sits on a different chain and would not repair the migration itself. Every fresh local or CI build from db/migrations would keep installing the INVOKER function, and the repository would carry two disagreeing statements of the same object.

SECTION_11_MUTATION_CONTRACT.requirement: Every mutation below must have a UNIQUE ANCHOR: applying it must turn RED a control that no other mutation in this table turns RED, so a green suite cannot be explained by a different control catching it. The implementer must record the anchor per mutation.

M1.mutation: Remove SECURITY DEFINER from the trigger function.
M1.expected: The POSITIVE insert goes RED with 42501 permission denied for SCHEMA AUTH, raised inside the PL/pgSQL body.
M1.falsifiability_premeasured: This is exactly the pre-remediation state measured at P1C, so M1 is known to be a real, reachable mutation and not a hypothetical.

M2.mutation: Remove SET search_path = public, keeping SECURITY DEFINER.
M2.SEMANTIC_ARM_REQUIRED: BINDING. A catalog-shape assertion alone is weak. MEASURED (P7A vs P7B): the shadowing attack only succeeds when the function OWNER can see the attacker-writable schema, so a naive semantic arm SILENTLY PASSES for the wrong reason and would read as 'the pin is unnecessary'. The semantic arm must therefore grant the owner USAGE on the shadow schema before asserting that the forged content_digest is accepted without the pin (P7B) and refused with it (P7C).

M3.mutation: Weaken the accepted_by_user_id equality (for example IS DISTINCT FROM to a nullable comparison, or drop the v_actor IS NULL arm).
M3.expected: The SPOOFED-ACTOR control and the ABSENT-IDENTITY control go RED.
M3.note: Both arms live in one IF at 0072:200; a mutation dropping only the NULL arm must still be caught, which is why absent-identity is a separate control.

M4.mutation: Remove the role-in-org invariant (the current_user_role_in_org exact-equality guard).
M4.expected: The NON-ADMIN-ACTOR and CROSS-TENANT controls go RED.

M5.mutation: Re-home the function to an owner lacking dependent-table reach in the test substrate.
M5.the_observed_error_is_the_TABLE_one: MEASURED (P5A, P5B): the failure is '42501: permission denied for table legal_instrument_versions' at PL/pgSQL line 5, NOT an auth-schema error -- and it stays the table error even after the thin owner is granted auth USAGE. A control written to expect an auth error under M5 will not fire.

M6.mutation: GRANT EXECUTE on the trigger function to a runtime role.
M6.note: The baseline is has_function_privilege(app, trigger_fn, EXECUTE)=f, measured at P3B while the positive insert succeeded -- so the control is falsifiable and the privilege is genuinely unnecessary.

M7.mutation: Restore the fixture GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA auth TO uellix_writer (fixtures line 125).
M7.note: This is the masking grant itself. P8A/P8B measured that restoring it makes even the UNREMEDIATED function pass, so this mutation guards the integrity of the whole suite, not one assertion.

M8.mutation: Skip journal SHA regeneration after amending 0072.
M8.note: The generator hashes WORKTREE bytes (scripts/journal-artifacts.ts reads with readFileSync utf8), so this mutation is detectable locally and in CI.

The journal generator hashes WORKTREE BYTES. In a worktree with core.autocrlf=true, 0072 materializes CRLF, its sha256 differs from the committed blob, and journal:verify / baseline:verify disagree for a reason that has nothing to do with the remediation. MEASURED in THIS worktree: core.autocrlf=false, 0 CR bytes in 0072, and worktree sha256 == git blob sha256 == e012b971... The implementer MUST verify this equality before and after the amendment.

The amendment is a header/footer restructure, not a two-line insertion, and the diff will touch both ends of the function.
